notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 5 simply supported 45-ft bays, W24X370 + MC18X42.7 girders, one 40-ton cab crane, on column caps over new W14X211 crane columns beside the existing W14X211 building columns (fixed bases, anchor rods and spread footings, crane-level rod X-bracing between the crane columns), with the rail, the top-flange ties and the column ties to the building columns, bearings and end stops; the building columns are checked for the tie forces with their existing load effects and carry no runway vertical load. The flexible plate on a direct flange saddle do not suit this capped girder (tie sizing ratio plate-tie-compression 8.83 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is the cap tieback angle bolted to the channel cap. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.reason: The flexible plate on a direct flange saddle do not suit this capped girder (tie sizing ratio plate-tie-compression 8.83 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is the cap tieback angle bolted to the channel cap.

No W and channel cap pair meets every sizing target; the closest: top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 2.49, vertical deflection 1.48 and lateral 1.36 of their limits; flanges at least 8.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 825 by cap channel fit, 130 by sizing ratio, 240 by flange width, 1 by AISC F13.2 proportions; the next lighter, W36X387 + C12X25: W flange too wide for the channel with the weld pocket and tie room. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios. A built-up plate girder is required: the closest section is built and calculated, and the package is a review draft

New crane column for a 40-ton crane (W12X65 to 7.5 t, W14X90 to 15 t, W14X109 to 30 t, else W14X132), fixed base, braced at the cap across the runway by the column tie and along it by the crane-level bracing. The W14X132 crane column gives a member (H1 or bracing web) or cap ratio above 1.00: the lightest heavier W14 whose member and bracing web pass, W14X211; its column cap ratios above 1.00 do not improve with a heavier column and are reported.

Fictitious example existing building column for a 40-ton crane (W14X90 to 7.5 t, W14X120 to 15 t, W14X159 to 30 t, else W14X211), checked for the tie forces with its existing load effects; replace with the surveyed shape.

selections.designed: combined with the building column, 150 in square; 156 in at the braced columns
selections.reason: Isolated 11.5 ft square crane-column footings 37.85 in from the building column would be 61.15 in into its 5 ft footing (6 in clear required): each crane column and its building column stand on one combined footing replacing the existing one, 12.5 ft square (13 ft at the braced columns), the building column shored and re-set on new anchor rods; sized for the base reactions; the braced columns' footing apart from the others' (the rods' uplift and shear along the runway), sliding resisted by the base friction and the soil's lateral bearing on the footing and its shear key (IBC §1806.3.1).

Column tie 0.625 in × 12 in with 3 1 in A325 bolts on sleeves in 1.688 in × 2.25 in vertical slots: the lightest within the 0.9 sizing target for the estimated column-tie force 70.102 kip (the girder bottom-flange force through the cap, bounded by the girder tie force estimate 67.224 kip; the crane column's eccentric top reaction 0.334 kip; the brace force 0.01P_r 2.544 kip; the calculation takes the bottom-flange force from the girder model) and its fatigue range 26.901 kip at all cycles; slot travel 0.275 in each way (the larger column shortening plus the erection tolerance).

Weld-on clip bases on the cap channel web are an AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1 attachment, Category D: the estimated top-plate range 23.02 ksi (rated-lift crane moment without impact plus the top-flange lateral bending under the side thrust) at all 500,000 cycles exceeds F_SR = 16.39 ksi (ratio 1.40, the project's all-cycle method). Bolted clamp plates leave holes for pretensioned bolts (item 2.2, Category B), as AISC DG7 and AIST TR-13 allow.

selections.designed: W24X370 + MC18X42.7, closest; plate girder required (outside the rolled/capped catalog)
selections.reason: Plate girder required: no W and channel cap pair of the catalog meets the girder sizing targets for this crane and span (the closest, W24X370 + MC18X42.7: top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 2.49, vertical deflection 1.48 and lateral 1.36 of the limits, screening estimates; targets ratio 0.85 and deflections 0.9). Design a built-up plate girder with a wide top flange (or a surge plate or lateral truss), or shorten the span; the configurator does not design plate girders.

fabrication.steel: W girder ASTM A992; cap channel and connection plates ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops. Cap: continuous fillet each W top-flange edge, with the end development shown. Full cap bearing contact required. Bearing stiffeners CJP to the W top flange, bottom fitted.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC. Capped girder shop sequence: weld and UT the bearing stiffener CJPs and any under-flange attachments, check the top flange flatness, then fit and weld the cap.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
